cues.zh: 但是

cues.zh: 对吧？每次你拿到新的信息，就得编造一套全新的接口来访问它，对吧？在 Java 里，这通常就是所谓的 JavaBean。但事实是，信息原本就只有几种基本形态。

cues.zh: 表现为 Map；表现为 Set。但千万别以这种形式暴露信息！因为一旦这么暴露，别人就能用现成的集合库去操作它们了。

cues.en: You don't want to do that. You've got to screw those guys. You've got to actually make a bean, you know, customer bean, an order bean, and all these things for which there is no extant API.
cues.zh: 你可不能让他们得逞。你得整整那些家伙。你必须实打实地造个 Bean，比如 CustomerBean、OrderBean 等等，全都是没有现成 API 可用的玩意儿。

cues.en: Then they have to make an API.
cues.zh: 这样他们就不得不自己去写一套 API。

cues.en: So encapsulate.
cues.zh: 所以，封装吧。

cues.zh: 封装

cues.en: is the complexity lover's friend.
cues.zh: 是复杂性爱好者的至爱。

cues.en: In particular, make sure people can never get access. We've kind of already covered setters.
cues.zh: 特别是，务必确保大家永远直接访问不到数据。关于 setter 我们差不多已经讲过了。

cues.en: Make sure people cannot get to the raw fact that they have associative data or that they have a set of data. They've got to go through beans. Your code base will automatically become an order of magnitude larger.
cues.zh: 确保大家接触不到本质事实——无论那是关联数据还是集合数据。他们必须通过 Bean 来访问。这样一来，你的代码库规模瞬间就能膨胀一个数量级。

cues.en: Right? Right there. Boom. And this is how we work already. So again, you're not going to be harmed. And the best part about it is the only argument for this is that it protects you from change.
cues.zh: 对吧？就在那儿。搞定。这就是我们现在的工作方式。所以再说一次，你不会因此受到伤害。最妙的是，支持这么做的唯一理由，就是它能保护你不受变化影响。

cues.en: But
cues.zh: 但是

cues.zh: 信息本身已经是一种抽象。

cues.en: Right? Sequences, maps, all those things, they're already an abstraction over what's going on underneath. So if you're gonna play that game I encapsulated to protect me from change, there's no point in stopping at one.
cues.zh: 对吧？序列、映射，所有这些东西，本来就是对底层运作方式的抽象。所以，如果你要玩“我封装起来，是为了保护自己不受变化影响”这套，那就没理由只封装一层。

cues.en: Mean why not encapsulate the encapsulations in case those change?
cues.zh: 我的意思是，为什么不把这些封装也封装起来，以防它们发生变化呢？

cues.en: And if you're gonna do that why don't you encapsulate the encapsulations of the encapsulations.
cues.zh: 既然要这么做，为什么不把这些封装的封装也封装起来呢？

cues.en: Right? There's there's absolutely no limit to the opportunity there. Now people are likely to figure you out if you do that. So you might wanna stick to just the one that's the industry standard, instead of additional ones.
cues.zh: 对吧？这方面的空间简直没有尽头。不过，你要真这么做，别人很可能会看穿你。所以你可能还是只用业界标准的那一种，别再额外加一层。

cues.en: Here's a really good one. Use static typing across subsystem boundaries. The across subsystem boundaries is important.
cues.zh: 这是个很好的例子：在子系统边界之间使用静态类型。这里“跨越子系统边界”很重要。

cues.en: So imagine back on our picture here, we have the little red guy who's gonna produce some data and the little blue guy who's eventually gonna
cues.zh: 想象一下，回到这张图上，有个红色小人要生成一些数据，而蓝色小人最终要

cues.en: consume some data. And there are a lot of intermediaries in between that don't care about the data at all until you add static typing to the mix. So the game here is to see how many intermediaries you can break.
cues.zh: 消费这些数据。中间还有很多中间环节，它们根本不关心这些数据，直到你引入静态类型。这里的玩法，就是看看你能让多少个中间环节出问题。

cues.en: And so the goal... And and think about it because everybody's gonna agree with you. Right? You can say look I'm... If if you're in a statically typed language already you can easily say look I'm I'm being very rigorous here. I'm I'm specifying exactly what I'm doing so that we don't have any bugs in our system. And you specify it so exactly that every intermediary has to know about it or they will fall over. Now,
cues.zh: 所以说目标是……想想看，因为大家都会赞同你。对吧？你可以说，看，我……如果你本来就在用静态类型语言，你可以轻松地说，看，我在这里非常严谨。我在精确说明我在做什么，这样系统里就不会有任何bug。你把它规定得如此精确，以至于每一个中间环节都必须了解它，否则就会崩溃。现在，

cues.en: you can do this with data but an even more beautiful way to do it is to do it with errors.
cues.zh: 你可以用数据做到这一点，但更漂亮的方式是用错误来做。

cues.en: And so the patterns here, there are a number of them and they all work by themselves but you can use them together. Use checked exceptions.
cues.zh: 所以这里的模式有很多种，它们各自都能独立工作，但你可以组合使用。用受检异常。

cues.en: Right? That makes everybody... It puts it in everybody's
cues.zh: 对吧？这让每个人都……它把这件事放进每个人的

cues.en: Use lots of different exception types. Look, we've thought through error handling really carefully. We've documented 50 different things that can go wrong of which the only mitigation strategy is you give up. But we've made them all different. We've made them all different. And then be very specific at the point where you throw
cues.zh: 用大量不同的异常类型。看，我们已经非常仔细地考虑过错误处理了。我们记录了50种可能出错的情况，而唯一的缓解策略就是你放弃。但我们把它们全都做得不一样。我们让它们全都各不相同。然后在抛出异常的地方非常具体，

cues.en: and very specific at the point where you catch.
cues.zh: 在捕获异常的地方也非常具体。

cues.en: Now, there's another piece to this which is very little known, which is that you should always, when you're doing this kind of thing, let unit testing expand your contract.
cues.zh: 现在，还有一点鲜为人知，就是做这类事情时，你应该始终让单元测试来扩展你的契约。

cues.en: So this is a beautiful thing. You're unit testing something,
cues.zh: 所以这很棒。你在对某个东西做单元测试，

cues.en: and your your documentation says, if I give you x,
cues.zh: 而你的文档说，如果我给你x，

cues.en: this will happen. And it doesn't say what happens if you'll give you y or z. Back in the good old days, we had that notion of being undefined. And people built systems, and you have to operate systems within their hardware parameters. So if you put the wrong voltage on it, the behavior is undefined. Right? You're not allowed to do that. But we don't want... Unit testing gives us this great opportunity
cues.zh: 就会发生这个。但它没说如果给你y或z会发生什么。在过去的好日子里，我们有“未定义”这个概念。人们构建系统，你必须在硬件参数范围内操作系统。所以如果你给它错误的电压，行为就是未定义的。对吧？你不允许那样做。但我们不想……单元测试给了我们一个绝佳的机会

cues.en: to come back in there and say, we're gonna make up a whole bunch of things that can go wrong at test time
cues.zh: 回过头来说，我们要在测试时编造一大堆可能出错的情况

cues.en: in in our mind. And we're gonna create separate tests for all of those when the only thing the user of the code could possibly do is abort.
cues.zh: 在我们的脑海里。我们要为所有这些情况创建单独的测试，而代码的使用者唯一能做的可能就是中止。

cues.en: Right? But we're gonna create 700 different flavors
cues.zh: 对吧？但我们会搞出700种不同的

cues.en: of abort and different tests for them. And I see this one in the Closure test suite all the time. It's really an excellent way
cues.zh: abort变体和各自的测试。我在Closure测试套件里老看到这个。真的，这是个绝佳的方式

cues.en: to make tests less useful is to add things that were never in the contract in the test suite.
cues.zh: 让测试变得没那么有用，就是在测试套件里加入那些从未出现在契约里的东西。

cues.en: Another thing you can do is put your language semantics on the wire. This is actually the thing that inspired me to call this narcissistic
cues.zh: 你还可以做的另一件事，就是把你的语言语义放到网络上。其实正是这件事启发了我把它叫做自恋式

cues.zh: 设计。这是我的语言语义，但我要把它们放到网络上。于是现在它们也成了你的语言语义，

cues.zh: 不管你喜不喜欢。而我们有着悠久的历史

cues.zh: 于是我们有了DCOM，有了Corba，有了Java RMI。

cues.zh: 而且

cues.zh: 是由像这类联盟组织构建的，它为网络通信建立了一套类型系统，因为我们有明确的证据表明类型系统能够扩展。

cues.zh: 我有两件事，你可能不太想听。

cues.zh: 它确实很简单。它做的事很少，也不挡你的路。所以，如果我们想把它对人搞复杂，就得换个方式对 JSON 下手。我们不能再用那套屡试不爽的办法，光让语言语义四处飘。我们其实可以搬出爱因斯坦的话：一切都要尽可能简单，但不能更简单。

cues.zh: 我们必须找出 JSON 太简单的那些方面。

cues.zh: 然后我们必须确保，这些不足

cues.zh: 在 JSON 里不是只停在某个序列化层，而是贯穿整个应用。

cues.zh: 我之前谈 setter 方法时，稍微提过或暗示过就地更新对构建复杂系统的好处。但当你跳出进程边界，继续

cues.en: Right? They're not ephemeral,
cues.zh: 对吧？它们不是用完就扔的，

cues.zh: 你知道，不是随手拿来又丢掉的东西。它们是放在某个壁橱或房间里的专用昂贵设备。

cues.zh: 在一个这些情况都成立的世界里，

cues.zh: 你就会设计就地更新，或者我所说的瞬态架构

cues.zh: 它们对并发访问是灾难性的，因为它们可能在你眼皮底下被改掉。访问模式必须始终是急切的，因为它可能在你眼皮底下变化。缓存非常麻烦，因为必须保持一致性，因为这东西可能在你眼皮底下变化。而且人人都在这么做。

cues.en: Now, there are a few things to avoid. You may have heard people talking about persistent data structures. Persistent data structures are designed for a world where memory is available in megabytes

cues.en: and gigabytes

cues.en: and machines are ephemeral and storage is cheap.
cues.zh: 而且机器是短暂的、存储很便宜。

cues.en: And so this really represents the world that has pertained for for many years now. You should avoid these things like the plague.
cues.zh: 所以这确实代表了多年来一直适用的世界。你应该像避瘟疫一样避开这些东西。

cues.en: And it's useful to remember what mutability is good for.

cues.zh: 再说一次，我不想在这个演讲里做那件事，但其他人可能会。

cues.en: And so it's useful to ask, what does mutability get used for in software? And it really gets used for three things. It gets used to model the substrate on which we run because it is mutable fundamentally.
cues.zh: 所以，问一问可变性在软件里到底用来干什么，是很有用的。它实际上用于三件事。它用来建模我们运行所依赖的底层环境，因为这个底层环境本质上是可变的。

cues.en: There's actual RAM that changes underneath.
cues.zh: 底下有真实的 RAM 在变化。

cues.en: Mutability
cues.zh: 可变性

cues.en: gets used to implement specific algorithms that are designed to say this thing changes as part of this algorithm.
cues.zh: 被用来实现特定算法，这些算法本来就设计成：这个对象会作为算法的一部分发生变化。

cues.en: And then mutability
cues.zh: 然后，可变性

cues.en: is used to implement a model of time.
cues.zh: 被用来实现时间模型。

cues.en: And an example of mutability
cues.zh: 而可变性

cues.en: being used to implement a model of time would be a git repository.
cues.zh: 被用来实现时间模型的一个例子，就是 git 仓库。

cues.en: Right? So there, you have mutability. Right? You can make more commits.
cues.zh: 对吧？所以那里就有可变性。对吧？你可以继续提交。

cues.en: But is git update in place?
cues.zh: 但 git 是原地更新吗？

cues.en: Not unless you're doing some really wonky admin thing. Right? So git maintains the full history or even multiple parallel histories of things that have happened in your application.
cues.zh: 除非你在做一些非常古怪的管理操作。对吧？所以 git 会保留你的应用中发生过的事情的完整历史，甚至多条并行历史。

cues.en: The good news for us as software developers is the reason that we do mutable o o has nothing to do with providing a time model. Right? Nothing in OO, nothing in Java or C sharp as it's typically used, provides you a way to answer interesting time model questions like what happened before what? What happened at the same time as what? What was the parent of this? What was the descendant of this?
cues.zh: 对我们软件开发者来说，好消息是：我们做可变 OO 的原因，和提供时间模型毫无关系。对吧？OO 里没有任何东西，Java 或 C# 的典型用法里也没有任何东西，能让你回答那些有趣的时间模型问题，比如什么发生在什么之前？什么和什么同时发生？这个的父级是什么？这个的后代是什么？

cues.en: The reason we use mutability is almost entirely bullet point one here, which is we're just using it because it's what we have.
cues.zh: 我们使用可变性，几乎完全是因为这里的第一点：我们只是因为它就是现成可用的，所以才用它。

cues.en: Right? It directly models the substrate we're running on. We need to keep doing that for as long as possible. Alright? This contributes more complexity to programs than anything else I've talked about today. So keep on keeping on.
cues.zh: 对吧？它直接建模了我们运行所依赖的底层基础。我们得尽可能一直这样做。好吧？它给程序带来的复杂度，比我今天讲过的任何东西都多。所以继续坚持下去。
